page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.cm4.6xlarge is a member of the High Clock Speed instance family running on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8369HB processor running at 3.2 GHz, featuring 12 physical cores and 24 dedicated vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. Cache configuration consists of 32 KB L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, and a 33 MB shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, and AES.

The instance delivers a balanced 1:4 CPU-to-memory configuration with 96.0 GB of system memory, equating to 4.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage architectures. Baseline network bandwidth is provisioned at 10 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate balanced middle-tier throughput across diverse computing tasks. The system records a PassMark CPU score of 24,266.27 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 9,204.0, complemented by a single-core score of 1,262.0. Memory throughput achieves 96.09 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 78.54 GB/sec for large-block writes. Key workload tests reflect 23.45 million Redis SET operations per second, 14.7 GB/sec static web serving throughput, and Clang compilation benchmarked at 20,182.0.

The ecs.cm4.6xlarge represents a standard general-purpose computing balance that combines dedicated multi-core capacity with sufficient memory density. Without local NVMe disks or discrete GPUs, resource overhead is focused on general compute execution. It fits mid-tier databases, static web serving tiers, software build and CI/CD pipelines, and small-to-medium CPU-based machine learning inference workloads.
